doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Heroin and the Miles Davis years
title: Miles's autobiography and the Yesterdays humiliation
summary: McLean judges Miles's portrayal of him accurate and recalls Miles shaming him on stage over a tune he hadn't learned, while Art Blakey told him to go learn it.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Are the representations he makes, or characterizations, you think, fair and accurate concerning you?

Miles gives his own interpretations of everybody in his own world. “Once upon a time,” by Miles Davis. That’s the way he is with everybody. Nobody comes up above a particular place, not even gods like Bird and Trane and those cats. It’s Miles’s own – I don’t want to even use an ugly word or anything like ego or make it bad, but it just is – that’s just the way he was. His assessment of me was accurate in terms of what it – historically, that it really happened, those things that he mentions in there.
Like his sort of prodding you over Yesterdays. You mentioned that.

Because I’m not afraid to tell about things that – I could have not said anything about that, when Quincy [Troupe] came to talk to me about doing the book for Miles. So but no, man. I thought that was a very important lesson that I learned from Miles at that particular time, because that one tune had almost got me fired, got me embarrassed on the stage in front of Duke Ellington and all these great people sitting in the audience. Miles got mad at me, went to the mic, and dropped a bomb on me, made me like a laughing

stock for a moment. I hated it. It brought me to tears. I was waiting in the alley out there, all swollen up and ready fight. Miles [sic: Art Blakey] said, “What are you getting ready to fight about? Miles told you to learn the tune. Man, you didn’t learn it. So what you mad about? Go learn it.”
Yeah, because Art was always like my big brother, somebody that I could learn a lot from. He always was like that with me.
